lessons.title: The one-page checklist
lessons.content:
# The one-page checklist

A tokenomics page is a sales document with numbers. Your job is not to decorate it. Your job is to copy it onto one page of your own, with blanks for everything the sales document skipped. If the page still has more poetry than integers after you are done, you have finished the exercise: the tokenomics were thin.

This checklist is the same for a blue-chip wrapper and for a brand-new BEP-20. Serious products fill more cells. That is information. Empty cells are also information. Do not fill them with hope.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to fill a one-page checklist with integers, addresses, and dates, and leave a cell blank rather than guessed.

## The cells

Write these rows, each with a source and a date:

1. Chain ID and contract 0x (chunked, from paper).
2. `decimals`, `name`, `symbol` as the contract reports them.
3. Max (code, comment, or “none”).
4. `totalSupply` raw and display.
5. Circulating as your subtraction, with the list, or “not computed.”
6. Mint, burn, pause, blacklist, tax, proxy admin — yes/no and who.
7. Top ten holders and labels you can defend.
8. Vests/lockers: amount, time, beneficiary, admin.
9. Emissions: units per day, mint vs treasury.
10. Liquidity: pair balances, LP holders, locker if any.
11. What the token legally is (if claimed): receipt, equity, points, unspecified list.
12. What you still do not know.

Twelve is enough. A forty-page PDF that does not fill these twelve is still empty.

## How to use the page without becoming a fan

You are not scoring charisma. You are not writing a buy thesis. You are producing a document you could hand to a future self who has forgotten the thread.

If cell 6 says mint is on and owner is an EOA, that fact outranks a paragraph about alignment. If cell 10 says pair inventory is small relative to treasury, that fact outranks “deep LP.” If cell 12 is longer than cell 4, you are doing it right.

Crystal Stones belongs on this page as a **drill**: address `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00`, chain 56. Fill what the explorer fills. Do not invent a mine in cell 11 because a logo is mineral-shaped. Cell 11 for an unspecified BEP-20 is often “a list.”

## What never goes on the checklist

Price targets. “Undervalued.” Seed phrases. Chat 0x addresses for tuition. Mentor “entries.” Rank-to-token conversion fantasies. Local-market folklore. A screenshot of a candle.

Tuition, if you are recording rails: $10 USDT BEP-20 on academy checkout. That is a school fact, not a tokenomics fact about CST.

## Worked refusal

A ten-slide deck skips contract address, names a max that is not in code, and ends on a rocket. You produce one page with blanks. You send the page back, or you send nothing. You do not complete their rocket with your money as homework. This school has no such homework.

TABLE
Cell | Filled by | Rejected filler
0x + chain | Paper + explorer | Chat paste
totalSupply | Read function | Rounded poster
Circulating | Your subtraction | A dashboard float
Controls | Verified source | “Renounced” sticker
Liquidity | Pair balances + LP holders | Padlock emoji
Legal claim | Documents | Logo shape
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
ONE PAGE
[identity] [supply three integers] [controls]
[holders]  [vests/locks]           [emissions]
[liquidity][legal claim]           [unknowns]
If unknowns > integers, the sales page was poetry.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
One page, dated, with blanks. Blanks are a result. Hope is not a cell.
ENDNOTE

## Order of operations, slowly

0x first, chain ID second, functions third, pie last. People do the pie first because it is pretty. Pretty is how you skip `mint`. Write by hand:

1. Chain ID and bookmarked explorer.
2. Token 0x, `name`, `symbol`, `decimals`, `totalSupply`.
3. Proxy? Implementation 0x?
4. `mint`, `burn`, `pause`, `blacklist`, `setFee`, `owner`, roles.
5. Vest and LP locker 0x if claimed.
6. Then, and only then, the pie, with addresses.

If step 4 is “too long,” the token is either huge or you are tired. Tired is a stop, not a skip.

## Date the page

Numbers stale. Functions can be upgraded if a proxy admin lives. A checklist without a date is a poster you will quote wrong next month. Write YYYY-MM-DD next to `totalSupply`.

NOTE
Academy rule: a tokenomics page without a contract 0x is advertising. Do not paste advertising into a memo as if it were a read.
ENDNOTE

## What a finished page looks like, as a template you copy by hand

Date. Chain ID. Token 0x. decimals. totalSupply raw and display. Proxy yes/no + implementation. owner / roles. mint cap or uncapped. pause. blacklist. tax + setter + max. vest 0x list. LP pair + locker. Circulating: named subtraction or “not evidenced.” Empty cells: price, minerals, ethics. Rails: tuition USDT BEP-20; CST verify-only. If a line is a screenshot, it does not go on the page.

## Say this out loud

- Copy tokenomics onto one dated page.
- Leave blanks; do not guess.
- Controls outrank alignment copy.
- Crystal Stones is a drill on chain 56.
- No price targets on the page.

Next: Crystal Stones figures as a drill.

lessons.title: Crystal Stones figures as a drill
lessons.content:
# Crystal Stones figures as a drill

Older materials around Crystal Stones may say about **135,000,000** total and about **104,100,000** circulating. Those sentences have been repeated until they sound like laws. They are not laws. They are historical marketing numbers. This lesson is the drill: how a literate reader treats those figures on the day they actually care, without turning the ticker into a long, a mine, or tuition.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to run the Crystal Stones supply drill on chain 56 and state what a match to an old poster does and does not mean.

## The only official identity this academy uses for the drill

Contract: `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00`.  
Chain: BNB Smart Chain, chain ID **56**.  
Role in this school: **verify-only**. Not a payment address. Not gas. Not a pair this course assigns.

Path: bookmark an explorer for BSC mainnet. Type the address from paper you wrote on a calm day. Do not connect a wallet. Read `name`, `symbol`, `decimals`, `totalSupply`. Convert raw to display. Write the display integer and the UTC date.

If a clone site asks you to connect to “sync circulating,” it is not an explorer.

## What match means

If `totalSupply` display on that day is consistent with ~135,000,000, you have **consistency on that integer** with older materials. That is all. You have not proven a mine. You have not received a buy order. You have not paid tuition. You have not learned circulating.

Circulating ~104,100,000 was always a subtraction. To repeat it you must list holders, decide which cannot `transfer`, and show the working. If a labelled lock moved, the old circulating number is a fossil. Fossils are useful. They are not live inventory.

If `totalSupply` does **not** match, you do not panic-trade and you do not invent a conspiracy as homework. You write the new integer, look for mint/burn/rebase, and update the memo. Methods over memory.

## What the drill refuses

- Treating the 0x as academy checkout. Checkout is $10 USDT BEP-20 on the academy page.
- Sending CST to the token contract as a “deposit.”
- Treating a match as mineral title.
- Treating a mismatch as a signal.
- Paying gas in CST. Gas is **BNB**.
- Handing a seed to “support” so they can “correct your circulating.”

Academy XP does not change because you completed a read. Ranks are database rows from study, not from holding.

## Worked scenario

You open the explorer on a Tuesday. You write: date, totalSupply display, decimals, whether source is verified. You compare to 135,000,000. Match or not, you add one line: “circulating not recomputed today” or you recompute it. You close the wallet-connect tab you never needed. You have finished the drill.

A cousin says “see, 104 million float, tiny.” You answer with the subtraction question. You do not answer with an order.

TABLE
Figure | Grade | Action
~135,000,000 total (old materials) | Marketing until it matches a live read | Read totalSupply
Live totalSupply display | On-chain fact that day | Date-stamp
~104,100,000 circulating (old materials) | A subtraction, possibly fossil | Recompute or write “not computed”
Match | Consistency on an integer | Not a mine, not a buy, not tuition
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
PAPER 0x  -->  explorer (BSC, 56)  -->  totalSupply / 10^decimals
COMPARE to ~135,000,000
   |-- match: consistency only
   +-- mismatch: new integer + mint/burn notes
Circulating 104.1m is a separate memo, not a field.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Match means the integer agreed that day. It does not mean a warehouse, a long, or a paid invoice.
ENDNOTE

## What a match would mean, said again with the actual 0x

On BSC chain 56, read `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00`. If `totalSupply` today equals a marketing number you were given, you have **consistency on that integer**, not a mine, not a warehouse receipt, not tuition, not a long. If it disagrees, you have a stale poster. Both outcomes are literacy. Neither is a trade.

Circulating around 104.1 million in older materials is a **claim**. Recompute: totalSupply minus named locked addresses you have actually checked can still `transfer`. If you cannot name them, write “circulating not evidenced.”

## What this drill refuses

No “undervalued versus minerals.” No FDV target. No “buy the discrepancy.” Discrepancy is a poster problem. Minerals are an RWA-course object. Checkout remains $10 USDT BEP-20. Gas is BNB. Staff will not ask you to send CST to “align supply.”

DIAGRAM
READ --> totalSupply, decimals, owner, mint/pause
COMPARE --> dated slide (optional)
WRITE --> match / mismatch / not evidenced
STOP --> no order
ENDDIAGRAM

## Holders tab is not circulating

Top holders on an explorer include pairs, lockers, CEX wallets, and unnamed EOAs. A pair holding tokens is inventory for swaps, not “locked from selling” in the vest sense — LP holders can pull. A CEX wallet is a company. Do not subtract a pair from totalSupply and call the rest circulating without saying so. Date the holder snapshot. Still no buy.

## Say this out loud

- Read totalSupply on chain 56 the day you care.
- Old 135 million is marketing until it matches.
- Old 104.1 million circulating is a subtraction.
- Match is not a mine, not a buy, not tuition.
- Gas is BNB; checkout is USDT BEP-20.

Next: FDV and ‘undervalued’ posters.

lessons.title: FDV and ‘undervalued’ posters
lessons.content:
# FDV and ‘undervalued’ posters

Fully diluted valuation is a multiplication: a price someone printed, times a supply someone chose. “Undervalued” is a feeling glued to that multiplication. This school will not give you a target and will not tell you a ticker is cheap. It will tell you which supply the poster used, and how a poster picks the smallest supply to make the multiplication look small — or the largest to make a rival look large.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to recompute FDV with max, total, and circulating as three different products, and refuse ‘undervalued’ as a tokenomics fact.

## Three products, not one FDV

Call P the last print on one venue for a tiny size. That P is already a local story (Trading & Markets). Tokenomics only asks: which integer did they multiply.

- P × circulating — often the smallest, used to look “cheap.”
- P × totalSupply — larger if burns/locks were excluded from circulating.
- P × max — larger still if a ceiling exists; undefined if uncapped.

Worked numbers (illustrative arithmetic, **not a target, not a quote**). Suppose a print of 0.10 quote-currency per unit. Circulating 200,000,000 → product 20,000,000. Total 800,000,000 → product 80,000,000. Max 1,000,000,000 → product 100,000,000. Same P. Three posters. The “undervalued versus a 20 million peer” poster used circulating and hoped you would not multiply the other two.

## Peers are not substitutes

Comparing two FDVs across tokens with different claims (a cash-flowing fund share versus an unspecified BEP-20 versus a meme list) is costume finance. Even two BEP-20s with similar holder counts are not peers if one has mint-on and one does not.

“Undervalued” requires a model of value. Tokenomics pages rarely have one. They have a multiplication and an adjective. Adjectives are not cells on your checklist.

## What this academy will not do

No “fair FDV.” No “CST should be.” No Mentor entry. If Mentor emits a target, report a malfunction. Crystal Stones remains verify-only. You may multiply integers in a memo. You may not treat the product as homework to buy.

Uncapped tokens make “fully diluted” a joke: fully is not defined. Rebase tokens make P × units a moving cartoon if units rescaled overnight.

## Worked refusal

A poster: “FDV only 20 million, still early.” You write the three products, the venue of P, the size at that print, and whether mint is on. If they cannot say which supply, you refuse “only.” You still have no order.

TABLE
Product | Supply used | How a poster abuses it
P × circulating | Memo integer | Smallest headline
P × totalSupply | Contract integer | Ignored when inconvenient
P × max | Ceiling or missing | “Fully” when it is not
P × fantasy | A wish | Entirely invented
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
P (one venue, tiny size)  ×  {circ 200m | total 800m | max 1,000m}
= three products, e.g. 20m / 80m / 100m in quote units
“Undervalued” is not a fourth product.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
FDV is a product of a local price and a chosen supply. ‘Undervalued’ is not a fourth integer.
ENDNOTE

## Float games at listing

Launch 5% circulating, rest “community.” Chart does 10× on the 5%. Headlines use the tiny market cap. FDV did not move with the same drama. Intermediate readers look at both columns: price × circulating, and price × max (or price × total if uncapped — then FDV is undefined or infinite in the honest sense).

## Undervalued versus what

Versus a cousin ticker? Versus a mine that is not in the token? Versus FDV of a different cap? “Undervalued” is a markets adjective this school will not assign. Tokenomics can only say: the poster used the small integer. Literacy is noticing. The empty box is the trade.

TABLE
Headline | Integer they multiplied | Integer they hid
“MC $1M” | price × 5% float | 95% that can unlock
“FDV cheap vs X” | a chosen cap | mint still on
“backed so undervalued” | a story | RWA four objects, later course
ENDTABLE

## Two multiplies, always

Market cap as used in headlines = price × circulating (and circulating was a memo). FDV = price × max, or price × totalSupply if they skip max. If mint is uncapped, FDV is not a number you can finish. Write “uncapped” instead of a fake FDV. A poster that shows only the small multiply is doing a float game. Noticing is literacy. Trading it is a desk — refused.

## Worked two-column scrape

Price 0.10. Circulating memo 10M. Max 100M. Column A: 0.10 × 10M = 1M (headline). Column B: 0.10 × 100M = 10M (FDV). If 90M unlocks into a 1M-float book, inventory dwarfs the book. Whether price falls is a market sentence. Whether the poster was complete is a no. Write both columns. Leave the verb “undervalued” off the page.

## Say this out loud

- Name which supply FDV used.
- Three supplies make three products.
- Undervalued is an adjective, not a cell.
- Uncapped tokens have no ‘fully.’
- No price targets from this school.

Next: what tokenomics cannot tell you.

lessons.title: What tokenomics cannot tell you
lessons.content:
# What tokenomics cannot tell you

A complete checklist is still a list about a token program and a set of wallets. It cannot see a warehouse. It cannot see a court. It cannot see next week’s print. People use tokenomics as a substitute for those other objects because the numbers are easy to screenshot. This lesson is a map of the edge of the subject so you stop asking it to do jobs it cannot do.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to name five questions tokenomics cannot answer, and park each in the right other drawer instead of forcing a pie chart to speak.

## Off-chain objects

**Is there a mine, a building, a barrel, an invoice?** Tokenomics will not know. That is the object drawer from RWA Specialization. `totalSupply` matching 135,000,000 does not weigh ore.

**Does a holder have a legal claim?** Tokenomics will not know. That is wrappers, prospectuses, indentures. A generous community slice is not equity.

**Will a court freeze the wrapper?** Tokenomics will not know. Pause on a token is a different freeze.

## Market objects

**What will the next print be?** Tokenomics will not know. Liquidity inventory tells you how thin the book is, not which way a taker will walk.

**Is this undervalued?** Tokenomics will not know. See the previous lesson.

**Is volume real?** Tokenomics will not know. Wash trading is a market-structure problem.

## Human objects

**Will the team sell?** A vest tells you when they *can*. It does not tell you when they *will*. Discretionary treasury is a key. Keys are held by people. People change.

**Is the chat sincere?** Tokenomics will not know. Sincerity is not a function.

Crystal Stones backing language (minerals, plus property and petroleum sentences) lives in the claim drawer. Tokenomics can only tell you how the list behaves. Keep the drawers apart.

## Worked refusal

A friend: “tokenomics are solid, so the asset is real.” You answer: solid tokenomics are arithmetic about a list. The asset is a separate memo. This school’s $10 does not purchase a conclusion about ore. It purchases lessons. You close the loop without a hymn.

TABLE
Question | Tokenomics can | Cannot
How many units exist today | totalSupply | Why they should exist
Who can mint | Source | Whether they are kind
When units unlock | Vest read | Whether they will sell
How thin the pair is | Balances | Next print
What the logo claims | Nothing | Mines, courts, cash flows
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
DRAWERS
token list  |  legal wrapper  |  object in the world  |  market print
Tokenomics lives in the first.
A pie chart that answers the other three is lying.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Tokenomics is arithmetic about a list. Do not hire it as a geologist, a judge, or a prophet.
ENDNOTE

## The empty cells are the course

Price. Ethics of the founders. Geology. Your tax lot. Whether you should hold. Leaving them empty is adult. Filling them from a Telegram voice note is how people get a second lesson they did not want.

Tokenomics tells you inventory policy: who can print, who can pause, who unlocks when, what a tax does to a transfer. It does not tell you that a consistent `totalSupply` makes a mineral real.

## Mentor must stay mute here too

If Mentor fills an empty cell with a target, it is a malfunction. Report it. Do not size it. The $10 you paid is for the checklist, not for a desk.

## Four questions to leave blank on purpose

1. Will the chart rise after the cliff? 2. Is the team honest? 3. Is the mineral pile real? 4. Should you hold? Question 3 belongs to RWA with four objects. Question 2 is not an explorer tab. Questions 1 and 4 are markets and preference. Filling any of the four from this lesson would turn the school into a shop. The $10 does not buy those answers.

## Why empty cells are a skill, not a lack of notes

Students fill cells because blank paper feels like failure. In this course blank is the grade for price, geology, and entries. A memo that answers those has left the syllabus. If you want geology, wait for RWA four objects. If you want a fill, you are in the wrong school function. Mentor filling the blank is a malfunction.

## Say this out loud

- A list is not a warehouse.
- A vest is ability, not intention.
- FDV is not value.
- Keep Crystal Stones claims in the claim drawer.
- Solid arithmetic is not a long.

lessons.title: Hidden mint and pause
lessons.content:
# Hidden mint and pause

The harms that look like “bad luck” are often functions that were always in the bytecode. Mint prints units to an address the holder did not vote for. Pause stops transfers while the story keeps talking. Either can hide behind a proxy, a second minter, or an unverified source. This lesson is how those functions hurt people who thought supply was a law.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to explain how mint and pause damage holders even when the chart is quiet, and what a literate memo records before anyone is hurt.

## Hidden mint

Hidden does not always mean obfuscated opcodes. It can mean:

- mint is in source but the website says “fixed supply,”
- mint sits in an implementation behind a proxy the website never mentioned,
- a minter role was granted to a new address after listing,
- a “bridge” minter on this chain prints while the other chain is a ghost.

Worked harm. Holder bought 1% of 100,000,000. Owner mints 100,000,000 to self. Holder still has the same units and now 0.5%. The wallet UI shows no outgoing transfer. The harm is share, then usually price as the new units hit a thin pair.

Record: `mint` present? who? cap? events this month? proxy?

## Pause

`pause` sets a flag so `transfer` reverts. Holders cannot sell on-chain. Pairs cannot swap. The chart on a company venue might still move if that venue uses an internal ledger — or it might halt. Pause is sold as a safety brake. It is also a trapdoor: inventory you cannot leave.

Who can pause? Owner? A “guardian”? A multisig you cannot name? Can they pause forever? Is there `unpause` only from the same key?

A paused token with an RWA story is especially cruel: the list freezes; the warehouse, if any, does not become yours.

## What verification actually buys you

Verified source lets you search for `mint` and `pause`. It does not stop an upgrade if a proxy admin exists. Unverified source means you cannot search; extra risk, not automatic guilt.

This academy will not dump a live function list for Crystal Stones that goes stale. You dump it the day you care on `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00` chain 56. Homework is read-only. No seed. No “support unpause.”

## Worked refusal

A chat: “owner minted to match new ore.” You ask for the reconciliation: ore in, tokens out, third party. Without it you have a mint plus a story. You do not send more units “to stay aligned.” You update cell 6 of the checklist.

TABLE
Function | Holder sees | Harm
mint to someone else | Share down, maybe no transfer row | Dilution into a thin book
pause | Transfers revert | Cannot leave
proxy upgrade | Bytecode changed | New mint/pause you did not re-read
unverified source | Nothing | You cannot even search
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
WEBSITE: fixed supply
BYTECODE: mint() onlyOwner
PROXY: admin can swap implementation
MEMO: supply is a policy with three doors.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Mint and pause are doors on the list. Websites are not doors. Read the doors.
ENDNOTE

## pause() and pairs

If `pause` blocks `transfer` to a pair, you cannot sell on the AMM. Buys may still occur from excluded addresses. The chart can print while you cannot exit. That is a tokenomics door, not a “market dump.” Read `paused()`, `pause()`, `unpause()`, and who holds `PAUSER_ROLE`.

## Hidden mint behind a role

`owner()` may be zero while `MINTER_ROLE` sits on a different address. AccessControl is a list. Count roles, not slogans. A proxy admin can point at new bytecode that mints even if the old implementation had no mint. Read the proxy, then the implementation, then the roles.

TABLE
Slot | If live | Honest sentence
mint / minter role | Supply is a privilege | Uncapped unless cap binds
pause / pauser | Exit can be switched off | Inventory with a gate
proxy admin | Bytecode can change | The ABI you read can die
ENDTABLE

## How you hunt a hidden minter in one sitting

Read the token. Search source for `mint`, `MINTER`, `issue`, `_mint`. Read AccessControl roles. Open the proxy admin. Open any “bridge” minter. List every address that can increase totalSupply. If the list is longer than the slide, the slide omitted a door. Pause: search `pause`, `whenNotPaused`, `stop`. If `transfer` to a pair is paused while `transfer` to an excluded EOA is not, the chart can still print. That is the door.

## Proxy admin as a mint with extra steps

Even with no `mint` on the implementation you read this morning, a proxy admin can `upgradeTo` bytecode that has `mint`. So a complete hunt includes: ERC-1967 admin slot, `ChangeAdmin` events, timelock or EOA. If admin is live, write “bytecode can grow a mint.” That is the honest max-supply sentence. Renounce on the old implementation does not bind the next one.

## Say this out loud

- Mint can steal share without a transfer row.
- Pause can trap inventory.
- Proxies hide future functions.
- Verified source is a search, not a halo.
- Ore stories do not explain a mint by themselves.

Next: blacklist and tax switches.

lessons.title: Blacklist and tax switches
lessons.content:
# Blacklist and tax switches

A blacklist is a mapping: this address cannot transfer. A tax switch is a variable: the gap on transfer changes when a privileged caller says so. Together they can turn a “2% ecosystem tax” into a 99% sell brick for selected people, or for everyone except the author’s wallets. Holders who only read the listing-day tax screenshot meet the switch later, in a queue they cannot exit.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to identify blacklist and variable-tax patterns and write the holder-level harm without using the word ‘community’ as a defence.

## Blacklist as a personal pause

Pause freezes everyone. Blacklist freezes chosen addresses. It is sold as anti-bot. It is also a way to trap a critic, a competitor, or a large holder who would sell. Some designs auto-blacklist the receiver of a transfer from a blacklisted address, spreading the freeze.

Worked harm. You are not blacklisted. You sell into a pair. Later the pair itself is blacklisted, or your address is, after you complained. `transfer` reverts. The units still show in `balanceOf`. The UI looks funded. The door is closed.

Record: `blacklist` / `deny` / `isBlocked` functions, who may call them, whether the pair is exempt.

## Tax switches

Listing: buy 1%, sell 1%. Source: `sellTax` is a public variable, `setFees(uint,uint)` onlyOwner, no cap. Month two: sell 25%. Month three: sell 49% for non-excluded. Excluded: owner, treasury, maybe the pair on buys.

Worked numbers. You send 100 toward a sell. Router plus 25% tax plus impact. Receiver side of the pool gets far less than the listing screenshot. The screenshot was not a covenant.

Some switches are time-limited in code (`if block.timestamp < launch+30 minutes then tax=99`). Those sniping taxes can be real. They can also remain callable. Read whether the high-tax branch can be turned back on.

## Honeypot cousins

A classic honeypot: buys work, sells revert, or sells exist only for excluded addresses. Tokenomics pages do not advertise this. The explorer’s “write” tab is not homework; a simulation on a fork, or watching whether other non-excluded addresses have ever sold, is closer to a read.

This school does not assign a honeypot test as a live sell. Watching others’ successful sell transactions is enough for a memo.

## Worked refusal

A stranger: “approve this tax-optimizer, sell tax becomes 0.” Approving a random spender is how inventories leave without a tax story. You do not approve. You do not give 2FA. You do not hand a seed to “whitelist your wallet.” Staff of this academy never ask.

TABLE
Mechanism | Listing caption | Later harm
blacklist(address) | Anti-bot | Selected holders cannot move
setFees unbounded | 1% / 1% | 25% sell for non-excluded
excludeFromFee | Fairness | Privileged dump path
approve optimizer | Lower tax | Drain
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
DAY 0: sellTax = 1%  (screenshot)
CODE:  setFees(uint) onlyOwner  // no cap
DAY 90: sellTax = 25% for non-excluded
EXCLUDED: owner, treasury
The screenshot was not the policy. The function was.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Blacklists and tax switches are personal and variable doors. Listing screenshots are not doors.
ENDNOTE

## USDT-class blacklist exists in serious tokens too

Centralised dollar tokens have freeze functions because they are company products. That is a disclosed counterparty. A meme with a hidden blacklist is the same function without the disclosure. Read `isBlacklisted`, `excludeFromFee`, `setFee`. Presence is information either way.

## Sell-tax flip as a delayed honeypot

Owner sets 1% at listing, 99% after a volume spike. You saw the 1% in a video. The setter was always there. Tokenomics grades the setter, not the video.

DIAGRAM
TODAY: fee = 1%, you buy
SETTER: setFee(99)
TOMORROW: you cannot leave without donating
The door was the setter, not the candle.
ENDDIAGRAM

## excludeFromFee is a privileged path

If the owner, the pair, or a “market maker” is excluded, they do not pay the tax you pay. That can be operational. It can also be an untaxed exit for insiders. You do not need to moralise. You need to write who is excluded. A video that shows a 2% sell from a non-excluded wallet does not bind the excluded wallets.

## Worked setter bound

Source shows `setFee(uint256 f)` with `require(f <= 100)` in percent. Then 100% is allowed. A comment that says “max 10%” is not the require. Write the require. If there is no require, write “unbounded.” Unbounded plus owner is a delayed honeypot even if today’s fee is 1%.

## Say this out loud

- Blacklist is a pause for chosen addresses.
- Unbounded setFees makes 1% temporary.
- excludeFromFee is a privileged path.
- Do not approve a tax-optimizer stranger.
- Staff never need your seed to whitelist you.

Next: calendars that are not code.

lessons.title: Calendars that are not code
lessons.content:
# Calendars that are not code

Tokenomics PDFs are full of dates: TGE, cliff end, “liquidity lock 1 year,” “emissions taper in Q3,” “team unlock 2027.” Some of those dates live in a contract. Many live in a slide. When a slide date slips, holders who treated the slide as bytecode discover that circulating arrived early — or that a promised burn never ran. The hurt is not that calendars change. The hurt is that people sized risk as if they could not.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to sort every dated promise into code, a legal document, or a slide, and refuse to subtract inventory on the strength of a slide.

## Three homes for a date

**Code** — a timestamp, a block number, a vesting contract. You can read it. Admins might still override (Module 2).

**Legal document** — a lock-up agreement, an employment contract, a securities legend. Courts might enforce it. Explorers will not. Token holders who are not parties may have no standing.

**Slide / tweet / roadmap** — a picture. It can be updated with another picture. Subtracting “team 15% until 2027” from circulating because a slide said so is how dashboards go stale on purpose.

Worked case. Slide: team locked 24 months. Explorer: team EOA sent 4,000,000 in month 3. Your circulating memo must add those 4,000,000 back. Arguing “but the roadmap” does not unsay the transfer.

## TGE as a calendar pile-up

Token generation event is a cluster of dates: first transferable token, first pair, first CEX IOU, first airdrop claim. They are not the same hour. A person who bought a points IOU thinking TGE meant instant circulating of a tiny float may meet: team unlocked at TGE, advisors unlocked at TGE, “ecosystem” unlocked at TGE. The slide’s cliff applied only to a slice too small to matter.

Write a table of slices versus TGE hour. If most slices are free at TGE, the cliff you were shown was decoration.

## Roadmaps as inflation schedules

“Q3 emissions decrease 50%.” If the emitter’s `setRate` is onlyOwner, Q3 is a hope. If the emitter’s rate is hardcoded and ownership is gone and there is no proxy, Q3 is closer to a fact. Grade the home of the date before you grade the intention.

Crystal Stones: this school will not maintain a public unlock calendar that pretends to be bytecode. If you care, you read holders and lockers on the day you care.

## Worked refusal

A countdown bot: “unlock in 3 days, prepare.” You check whether a locker actually pays then. If the bot is counting a slide, you mute the bot. You do not pre-position a trade as homework. This course still has no entries.

TABLE
Date | Home | May slip?
Cliff in vesting.sol | Code | If admin/revoke/proxy
Exchange lock-up letter | Legal | If parties agree; you may not be a party
“Team locked 2027” PNG | Slide | Yes, silently
TGE tweet | Slide | Definition of TGE moves
Emitter setRate Q3 | Code if hardcoded; else slide | Owner joystick
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
SLICE        SLIDE SAID         EXPLORER SAID AT TGE
team 15%     cliff 24 mo        4,000,000 moved month 3
advisors 5%  cliff 12 mo        transferable at TGE
ecosystem 20% “rewards later”   EOA, no vest
MEMO: subtract only what code still traps.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
If the date is not in code or in a document you can name, it is a slide. Do not subtract slides from circulating.
ENDNOTE

## Google sheets

If the unlock schedule is a sheet an intern can edit, it will be edited. Export a copy with a date if you must cite it. Do not cite it as bytecode. A Notion page is the same species. A tweet thread is worse.

## “Audit coming” is not a calendar

A date on a slide for an audit, a listing, or a burn event is marketing time. It does not bind `mint`. Tokenomics only binds what the contract binds. Put marketing dates in a second column labelled “unenforceable.”

## How to cite a sheet without becoming its believer

If you must mention a public unlock sheet: export, hash or at least date-stamp, quote the row, and write “unenforceable.” Then try to find a vest 0x that matches the row. If none matches, the sheet is the whole evidence. That sentence is allowed. “The unlock is coded because a sheet exists” is not.

## Marketing time versus block time

“Burn event Friday.” Friday is a timezone. Blocks are numbers. If no txhash appears, Friday was a caption. “Listing next month” does not disable `mint` this month. Keep two columns on the memo: enforced (functions, timestamps in code) and announced (everything else). Only the first column is tokenomics.

## Say this out loud

- Dates live in code, law, or slides.
- Transfers beat roadmaps.
- TGE is several hours mashed into one word.
- Owner-set emission tapers are hopes.
- Countdown bots are not lockers.

Next: airdrop and TGE rugs.

lessons.title: Airdrop and TGE rugs
lessons.content:
# Airdrop and TGE rugs

Airdrops and token-generation events concentrate three tokenomics failures into a short window: unmapped allocations become transferable at once, liquidity is thin, and a crowd is trained to sign anything that looks like a claim page. The hurt is often not a novel function. It is the checklist from Module 4, ignored on a loud day.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to list the tokenomics tells of an airdrop or TGE that will harm claimants, and refuse claim sites that need a seed or a wild approval.

## What an airdrop actually is

A distributor contract, or a manual set of transfers, credits addresses from a list. The list is off-chain until the credit happens. Points seasons (Module 3) become tokens only at this step, and only if the operator follows through.

Tells that the drop is inventory, not a gift:

- A large share of “airdrop” sits in the operator’s wallets.
- Claim requires `approve` of an unrelated spender, or a signature typed as “permit everything.”
- Tax on claim is 50% to a marketing EOA.
- Pair inventory is tiny relative to the claimable amount.

Worked numbers. Claimable 20,000,000. Pair holds 500,000 plus a thin quote side. If even 10% of claimants sell, they walk a cliff. The “fair drop” was a queue into a kiosk with almost no stock.

## TGE rugs that are tokenomics, not magic

Classic pattern: public was told circulating would be small; at TGE, team, advisors, and “ecosystem” can all transfer; LP is pulled after the first print (LP tokens were never locked); mint still on; tax switch on sells. Each piece was a cell on the checklist. The loud day made people skip cells.

A points-to-token conversion that silently moved from 10:1 to 100:1 is an IOU rewrite. People who bought points in a grey market discover they purchased a row.

## Claim-page impersonation

The most reliable harm at TGE is not even the token: it is a clone claim site. Seed, 2FA, remote control, “connect to check allocation.” This academy’s staff never ask. Official claim, if a project runs one, is a URL you typed from a calm bookmark — and this school still does not assign you to claim CST. Verify-only means read. It does not mean hunt airdrops as homework.

Gas to claim on BSC is **BNB**. A site that wants CST first to “activate claim” has already failed.

## Worked refusal

A DM: “TGE claim, last 20 minutes, paste seed to sync.” You do not paste. You do not argue. You report. You open nothing from the DM. If you ever verify Crystal Stones, you use the paper 0x on a bookmarked explorer, chain 56, and you stop. Tuition remains $10 USDT BEP-20 on checkout, not a claim portal.

TABLE
Tell | Why it hurts
Claimable >> pair inventory | Queue into a thin book
LP unlocked at TGE | Inventory can vanish
Conversion rate moved | IOU rewritten
Claim needs seed or infinite approve | Drain
Team transferable at TGE despite cliff PNG | Slide was not code
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
LOUD DAY
points --> claim site (clone?) --> token credit --> thin pair
Break the chain at the clone.
Never seed. Never remote control.
Checklist cells still exist at TGE. Especially then.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Airdrops are inventory events. TGE is a loud day for the same checklist. Seeds are never part of a claim.
ENDNOTE

## Merkle claims

Real claims often use a merkle proof: your address is in a tree; you pass a proof; the contract mints or transfers. Hostile sites wrap that UI and add `approve` on USDT. A merkle proof does not need your seed. If they ask for one, stop. If they ask for `setApprovalForAll` or an infinite USDT approve, you are not claiming. You are loading a gun.

## TGE that is a new 0x

“Migration to V2” at TGE is a new contract. All the tokenomics reads start at zero: mint, pause, tax, owner. Treat it as a first read, not a continuation. Crystal Stones does not become tuition at a TGE. Checkout stays USDT BEP-20.

## Claim UI versus claim contract

Bookmark the claim 0x from documentation you saved on a calm day. The UI must call that 0x with `claim` or `harvest` or a merkle function. If the UI’s first call is `approve` on a different token, leave. If the UI wants you to import a seed to “prove eligibility,” leave. Eligibility is an address on a list, not a phrase.

## New 0x at TGE, checklist restart

V2 token is a new contract. Your V1 reads do not carry. Start: chain ID, 0x, decimals, totalSupply, mint, pause, tax, owner, proxy. Migration UI that asks `approve` on V1 to a router you have not bookmarked is a drain path. Migration that `burn`s V1 in a contract you read and `mint`s V2 to the same msg.sender is a migration. Decode. CST is not a TGE homework asset. Verify-only remains.

## Say this out loud

- Claimable size versus pair size is the first ratio.
- LP that can be pulled is not a floor.
- Conversion rates can move before TGE.
- Clone claim sites harvest seeds.
- This school assigns no CST claim.

Next: Module 6 — practice and refusals.

lessons.title: Write the memo
lessons.content:
# Write the memo

Literacy that stays in a quiz is a costume. This lesson is the one-page memo you can actually produce: identity, three supply integers, controls, locks, liquidity, emissions, taxes, unknowns. You will write it on a generic token first, then you may run the Crystal Stones drill as identity-plus-totalSupply only. You will not write a hymn. You will not write a target.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to produce a one-page tokenomics memo with dated integers and a blank-heavy unknowns list, without a buy or sell sentence.

## The template

Header: name as the contract reports it, 0x chunked, chain ID, date, explorer used.

Supply: max / total display / circulating (or “not computed”), decimals, raw totalSupply.

Controls: mint, burn, pause, blacklist, tax (buy/sell/transfer), proxy admin — each yes/no/unknown, with caller.

Inventory schedule: top holders you checked, vests/lockers with four fields or “none found,” emissions units/day or “none found.”

Market inventory: pair address if any, both balances, LP holders, locker on LP or not.

Taxes: receiver-gets-X-on-100, destinations, switches.

Unknowns: the longest section if you were honest.

Forbidden last line: anything that says buy, sell, fair value, or “load.”

## Worked generic memo (numbers are a drill, not a ticker)

Date D. Chain 56. Decimals 18. Max none found. totalSupply display 80,000,000. Circulating not computed (holder list unfinished). Mint yes, onlyOwner EOA. Pause yes. Blacklist unknown (source unverified — extra risk). Tax 5% to marketing EOA, setFees unbounded. Pair holds 2,000,000 token + 40,000 quote. LP in team EOA. Emissions 50,000/day minted.

Unknowns: legal claim, locker for team 15% slice (PNG only), whether marketing EOA is also “community.”

This memo already forbids the sentence “tokenomics are clean.”

## Crystal Stones line in the memo

If you include CST: identity `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00` chain 56, verify-only. totalSupply as read that day versus older ~135,000,000 marketing. Circulating ~104,100,000 only if you recomputed. Match = consistency on the integer. Not a mine. Not a buy. Not tuition. Rails sentence: Intermediate is $10 USDT BEP-20 on academy checkout; gas is BNB; no seed.

## How you know you are done

Another reader could re-run your reads without your chat history. If they would need a voice note to understand a cell, the cell is still poetry. Ranks and XP do not belong in the memo as token supply. They are database rows.

TABLE
Section | Must include | Must not include
Header | 0x, chain, date | A candle
Supply | Three integers or blanks | A rounded vibe
Controls | Function + caller | “Aligned team”
Unknowns | Explicit list | Filled-in hope
Close | No order | A target
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
MEMO PAGE
identity --> supply --> controls --> inventory --> taxes
unknowns (longest if honest)
last line: no buy, no sell, no fair FDV
CST optional drill: read, date, compare 135m, stop.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
A memo is dated integers plus unknowns. If it ends on a rocket, it is not this assignment.
ENDNOTE

## One sitting, one page, dated

If the memo takes three hours, the token is either huge or you are decorating. One hour, one page, date, stop. Include: 0x, chain 56 or 1, decimals, totalSupply, mint/pause/tax/owner, vest, LP locker, what you did not find. Empty cells beat invented ones.

## What not to put on the page

A target price. A mineral grade. A “team is based.” A screenshot of a candle. Those belong to other courses or to nowhere. This academy will not grade your memo as a trade idea.

## Length and what “done” means

Done means: another student could re-read your 0x and get the same functions. Done does not mean: a recommendation. If you wrote “looks bullish” you are not done — you are off the course. Strike that line. Leave the empty cells empty. Date. Stop.

## Hand copy, not a screenshot collage

Type the 0x. Type chain 56 or 1. Type function names you opened. Screenshots of pies without 0x do not count. If your page is three GIFs, it is not a memo. One sitting. Date. Empty cells labelled empty. Then close the explorer. More clicking is how people import a bait token “just to see.”

## Say this out loud

- One page, dated, re-runnable.
- Blanks beat guesses.
- CST line is verify-only if present.
- No buy sentence.
- XP is not a supply integer.

Next: refuse five posters.

lessons.title: Refuse five posters
lessons.content:
# Refuse five posters

You will meet the same five posters for the rest of your reading life. Each one is a compressed lie about a cell you already have. This lesson is spoken refusals — short enough to say, precise enough to be tokenomics rather than mood.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to refuse five standard tokenomics posters in one sentence each, naming the missing cell.

## Poster 1 — tiny float

“Only 104 million circulating, tiny float.” Refusal: circulating is a subtraction; show the wallets you removed and whether they can still transfer. If this is the Crystal Stones fossil figure, add: I will not use 104,100,000 unless I recompute it the day I care. Missing cell: subtraction list.

## Poster 2 — burned forever

“50% burned, ultra scarce.” Refusal: mint minus burn over the same window, plus whether the burn address can send, plus whether mint still exists. A ceremony is not a net. Missing cell: net issuance.

## Poster 3 — LP locked 100 years

Refusal: pair balances, LP token holders, locker four fields, treasury sitting outside the pair. A padlock emoji is zero fields. Missing cell: LP locker read.

## Poster 4 — undervalued FDV

Refusal: which supply did you multiply, on which venue’s tiny print, and why is a different list a peer. This school still has no target. Missing cell: the chosen supply and the adjective’s model — the model does not exist.

## Poster 5 — claim / tax-optimize / pay CST to unlock

Refusal: tuition is $10 USDT BEP-20 on academy checkout; CST is verify-only; I will not seed, approve a stranger, or pay the token contract. Missing cell: this was never tokenomics; it was a drain wearing a pie chart.

Say them out loud later in this lesson. Then write them on paper. A refusal you cannot say will not survive a loud TGE.

TABLE
Poster | Missing cell | One-line refuse
Tiny float | Subtraction list | Circulating is a memo
Burned forever | Net mint-burn | Ceremony ≠ policy
LP 100 years | Locker fields | Emoji ≠ lock
Undervalued FDV | Which supply × which P | Adjective ≠ integer
Pay CST / seed | Rails | Checkout is USDT; no seed
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
FIVE POSTERS --> FIVE CELLS
float --> subtraction
burn --> net
LP --> locker
FDV --> which supply
claim --> rails (USDT, no seed)
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Five posters, five missing cells. Mood is not a sixth cell.
ENDNOTE

## Poster 6, free, because it always shows up

“Audit coming” is not `mint` disabled. “Audit done” is a PDF with a scope. Scope that excluded owner mint is a punchline. “Renounced” while proxy admin lives is a costume. “LP locked” without a locker 0x is a caption. “Undervalued RWA” is four objects you have not evidenced. Keep them off the page.

## Poster: “code is law” as a supply story

A revert on mint-over-cap is law-of-the-contract. A court order on a company wrapper is law-of-a-country. Both exist. A poster that says only one exists is selling something. Tokenomics reads the first. RWA course reads the second. Do not mash.

## The five, restated as doors

1. “Max supply” without a binding cap. 2. “Renounced” with a living proxy admin or minter role. 3. “LP locked” without a locker 0x. 4. “Audit” with a scope that skipped owner mint. 5. “Undervalued RWA” without four objects. Each is a door you already have a name for. Refusing is the skill. Debunking without a read is fan behaviour in reverse — also refused.

## Refusing without becoming a prosecutor

You do not need to call a team a scam to refuse a poster. You need: “cap not binding,” “admin live,” “locker not found,” “scope skipped mint,” “RWA objects not named.” Those sentences travel. Insults do not. This academy grades the sentences. It does not grade your anger.

## Say this out loud

- Tiny float needs a subtraction list.
- Burns need a mint column.
- LP locks need four fields.
- Undervalued is an adjective.
- CST is not checkout and not a seed ritual.

Next: never-list.

lessons.title: Never-list
lessons.content:
# Never-list

A never-list is not a personality. It is a set of actions this academy will not ask for and that you should treat as hostile if someone else asks while wearing this school’s logo. Tokenomics study produces curiosity. Curiosity is not a licence. Write the list so a loud day cannot edit it.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to recite the never-list for tokenomics study and mark any staff request that contradicts it as an impostor.

## Never do these in the name of this course

Never send a seed, private key, 2FA code, or remote-desktop access.

Never pay Intermediate in Crystal Stones, in BNB to a chat, or to the token contract. Pay **$10 USDT BEP-20** on the academy checkout page if you pay.

Never connect a wallet to a clone explorer, locker UI, or airdrop portal to “prove” a read. Reads do not need signatures.

Never treat Mentor as a desk: no entries, no targets, no “easy 2%.”

Never buy or sell ranks, XP, or certificates. They are database rows.

Never send CST to “reduce tax,” “whitelist,” “mint Adept,” or “sync circulating.”

## Never write these in a memo

Never a price target. Never “undervalued.” Never “guaranteed unlock.” Never “the mine backs this integer.” Never a local-market exception (this is a global school of methods, not a travelogue). Never a person’s name as if it were a function.

Never paste someone else’s 0x from a DM as identity. Paper from a calm day, or nothing.

## What you may do

Read. Date-stamp. Fill blanks. Recompute circulating if you want, with working. Compare 135,000,000 only as a consistency check on `totalSupply` at `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00` chain 56. Close the explorer. Keep gas as BNB in your own wallet for your own reasons — this course still does not assign a transfer.

## Worked refusal

A profile with a crystal avatar: “Academy support, send 12 words to reset vesting.” You already have the never-list. You do not negotiate. You report. You do not test whether they are “the real team.” Staff never ask.

TABLE
Never | Why | Impostor costume
Seed / 2FA / remote | Custody death | “Support reset”
Pay CST for Intermediate | Wrong asset, wrong address | “Discount if you hold”
Connect to prove a read | Drain | Clone explorer
Buy ranks | Rows, not tokens | “Mint Adept”
Price target in memo | Not this subject | Mentor malfunction
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
NEVER-LIST (paper)
no seed  no CST tuition  no clone connect
no rank market  no targets  no mine-from-integer
YES: read, date, blank, close
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
If a request needs a seed, a CST payment, or a target, it is not this course.
ENDNOTE

## Selling ranks and fake TGEs

Anyone offering to sell Adept, a “governance NFT,” or a Crystal Stones academy token allocation is impersonation. Same never-list as the landing page: seed, 2FA, remote control, CST as tuition, chat 0x as checkout.

## Approvals at claim sites

A claim that requires infinite USDT approve is a drain. A claim that requires a seed is a drain. A claim that is just `claim(proof)` on a bookmarked contract is a claim. Decode.

## Tokenomics-shaped impersonation

“Send CST to this 0x to burn and receive 2×.” “Update your allocation by connecting here” (approve). “Academy rank mint.” “We need your seed to whitelist the vest.” All never-list. Real vests pay a beneficiary already in the contract. They do not need your phrase. Checkout remains $10 USDT BEP-20 on the academy origin.

## Seed for a vest, decoded

A vest already knows its beneficiary. A site that needs your seed to “attach the vest” is stealing the factory, not helping the cliff. Same for 2FA “to whitelist.” Whitelists are address lists. Checkout never needs a seed. Staff never need a seed. CST never pays the $10.

## Say this out loud

- Seeds are never classwork.
- Checkout is USDT BEP-20 on the academy page.
- Reads do not need a signature.
- Ranks are rows.
- No targets in the memo.

Next: close.

lessons.title: Close
lessons.content:
# Close

You entered this course because posters print integers the size of a headline. You leave with three supply numbers, a net of mint and burn, a vest that is inventory, a tax that is a gap plus a switch, a checklist, a Crystal Stones drill that refuses to become a religion, and a never-list. That is the whole purchase. It is not a position.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to close the course by restating the rails, the CST drill, and the job of a tokenomics memo — then stop.

## What you can do tomorrow

Open any tokenomics page. Copy it onto one dated page. Fill identity, three integers, controls, locks, liquidity, emissions, taxes, unknowns. Refuse the five posters. Do not buy. Do not sell. If the page is Crystal Stones, read `totalSupply` at `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00` on chain 56. Compare to ~135,000,000 only for consistency. Do not recompute 104,100,000 unless you have a subtraction list. Stop.

## Rails, last time

Intermediate is **$10 USDT BEP-20** on academy checkout. Crystal Stones is **verify-only**. Gas on BSC is **BNB**. Staff never ask for a seed, a key, 2FA, or remote control. Academy XP and ranks are **database rows**, not tokens. Certificates are academic. Mentor is a tutor; a target from Mentor is a malfunction.

This course will not tell you to farm, claim, or hold CST. Matching an integer is not tuition.

## What tokenomics was for

So that a list cannot masquerade as a warehouse, a calendar, a court, or a payday. So that dilution, pause, blacklist, and tax switches have names before they have victims. So that FDV cannot hide which supply it used. So that points stay rows.

If you wanted a hymn, you are in the wrong building. If you wanted a desk, the signal box is empty on purpose.

## Worked close

You close the explorer tab. You put the memo in a folder with a date. You do not set an alert that looks like an entry. You go study the next Intermediate course, or you go outside. Either is more adult than refreshing a pie chart.

TABLE
Keep | Drop
Dated totalSupply | Fossil circulating without working
Four-field locks | Padlock emoji
Net mint-burn | Burn ceremony video
Unknowns list | Undervalued
USDT checkout rail | CST-to-contract payment
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
END OF COURSE
read --> memo --> refuse --> never-list --> stop
CST: verify-only, chain 56, match ≠ mine ≠ buy ≠ tuition
$10 USDT BEP-20. Gas BNB. No seed.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
The course ends on a stop, not on an order. Integer literacy is the product.
ENDNOTE

## Carry-forward into markets

You now have inventory calendars: three integers, net mint-burn, vests, taxes, emissions, a CST drill that stops at match/mismatch. Markets course will talk fills without turning those calendars into a signal. Keep the drawers apart. The $10 was for the drawers.

## What you carry, one screen

Three integers, dated. Net mint-burn between two blocks. Vest 0x or “no vest.” Tax setter or “no tax.” Pause/blacklist/mint roles. CST drill: match or mismatch, then stop. Empty: price, minerals, entries. Next Intermediate courses use these objects; they do not replace them with a candle or a DAO slogan.

## Stop rule, recap as a card you could tape

totalSupply — read, dated.
circulating — memo or “not evidenced.”
mint / pause / tax setter / proxy admin — named or “absent.”
vest / LP locker — 0x or “absent.”
CST — verify 0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00 chain 56; match ≠ buy.
Tuition — $10 USDT BEP-20.
Price — empty.
Then the next course.

## Say this out loud

- Three integers, dated.
- Match is consistency, not a long.
- Tuition is USDT on checkout.
- Ranks are rows.
- Stop.

Next: the next Intermediate course, with the same rails.
